question: A tank in the shape of a hemisphere is filled with water. The water is then transferred to a cylindrical container with the same radius. What fraction of the cylinder is filled?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume ratio of a Hemisphere to a Cylinder with the same radius and height (H = R) is always 2 : 3.

Volume of Hemisphere = 2/3 × (πR³)

Volume of Cylinder = 1 × (πR³)

Fraction filled = (2/3 πR³) ÷ (πR³) = 2/3

**∴ The correct answer is 2/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Radius of hemisphere = R; Radius of cylinder = R; Height of cylinder H = R (to accommodate the hemisphere's volume ratio).

Formula Used: Volume of Hemisphere (Vₕ) = (2/3)πR³; Volume of Cylinder (V꜀) = πR²H

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0ca1b32c4299cd02784d974861d55592af6fa77d2a7091310d5f87bf08dee64b.png] 

⇒ Let the common radius be R.

⇒ Volume of water in hemisphere = (2/3) × π × R³

⇒ Capacity of the cylinder (with height H = R) = π × R² × R = πR³

⇒ Fraction filled = (Volume of water) ÷ (Capacity of cylinder)

⇒ Fraction filled = [(2/3) × πR³] ÷ [πR³]

⇒ Fraction filled = 2/3

**∴ The correct answer is 2/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of Sphere

A full sphere has a volume of (4/3)πR³, which is exactly double that of a hemisphere.

Volume of Cone

For a cone with the same radius and height (H = R), the volume is (1/3)πR³, which is half the volume of a hemisphere.

Surface Area of Hemisphere

Curved Surface Area = 2πR² and Total Surface Area (including base) = 3πR².

Archimedes' Ratio

The ratio of volumes of a Cone, Hemisphere, and Cylinder (all with same R and H=R) is 1 : 2 : 3.</p
